name: New antisemitism
summary: New antisemitism is the claim that hostility to Jews has taken a new form since the late twentieth century, directed at Israel as the 'Jew among nations'. Its proponents hold that denying Israel's right to exist, demonizing it, or judging it by standards applied to no other state is antisemitism, whether it comes from the far left, Islamism or the far right. Critics reply that this blurs criticism of a state with prejudice against a people.
scope: The mainstream proponent position as formulated by Natan Sharansky (the 3D test), Irwin Cotler (nine aspects), Robert Wistrich and the ADL tradition, and as codified in the IHRA working definition and its Israel-related examples. Excludes critics such as Klug, Finkelstein and Lerman, and the Jerusalem Declaration camp. Because it is a thesis about antisemitism rather than a full programme, most answers on economics and unrelated domestic issues are low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: Natan Sharansky
keyFigures.role: Formulated the 3D test for telling antisemitic from legitimate criticism of Israel.

keyFigures.name: Irwin Cotler
keyFigures.role: Canadian jurist who lists nine aspects of the new antisemitism.

keyFigures.name: Robert Wistrich
keyFigures.role: Historian who argued that equating Zionism with Nazism is a feature of the new antisemitism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The concept concerns antisemitism, not health policy; its adherents span left-liberal to conservative, so no common line can be inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage policy is unrelated to the new-antisemitism argument and proponents divide along ordinary party lines.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Not addressed; proponents include both social democrats and market conservatives, so the answer is genuinely split.

public-ownership.rationale: No stated position; the idea is held by people on both sides of the public-ownership debate.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Taxation is not part of the doctrine; adherents are split across the economic spectrum.

unions-good.rationale: Never discussed in the sources; proponents are mixed on labor policy.

property-fundamental.rationale: Not addressed; liberal and conservative proponents would differ on how strong property rights are.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Corporate regulation is outside the concept; proponents split on it.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; mainstream Jewish communal organizations that advance the concept generally support a social safety net, so a mild disagree is inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not discussed; proponents want antisemitic terror countered but are split on civil-liberty trade-offs.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Unrelated to the doctrine; adherents split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Cotler warns that defining antisemitism should not preclude free speech, while others back hate-speech laws, so proponents are split.

strong-leader.rationale: Proponents frame the cause as defending liberal-democratic values, which suggests wariness of leaders bypassing institutions.

state-harmful.rationale: Sharansky's plea for governments to act against antisemitism assumes states are necessary and beneficial.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split along their national political lines.

empower-police-military.rationale: Security of Jewish sites is a concern, but the sources take no general position on police powers.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Unrelated to the concept; adherents split.

decide-locally.rationale: Not addressed; no inference possible from the sources.

rehabilitation.rationale: Criminal justice philosophy is not addressed; adherents split.

traditional-family.rationale: Not addressed; proponents include religious conservatives and secular liberals.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not part of the concept; adherents are divided.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between religious and secular.

more-religion-public.rationale: The concept is framed in universal-rights terms and its Western proponents mostly favor a secular public square, so a mild disagree is inferred.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; proponents dispute especially whether anti-Zionist anti-racism movements are fair, so no common line.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Not addressed directly; proponents are split between civic and cultural conceptions of nationhood.

gradual-change.rationale: No stated position on the pace of change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Some proponents tie new antisemitism to Muslim immigration in Europe (Fischel) while others reject that framing, so they are split.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Sharansky argues that the UN singles Israel out while ignoring China, Iran, Cuba and Syria, which makes adherents distrustful of giving it more power.

nation-first.rationale: Not addressed; proponents stress democratic solidarity but also Israel's self-reliance, so split.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Sharansky calls on the free world to confront antisemitism with moral clarity, which suggests openness to acting on human rights, inferred only.

open-borders.rationale: Proponents defend a Jewish state with a defined national character; open borders as a goal is inferred to be disfavored.

limit-growth.rationale: Degrowth is unrelated to the concept.

revolution-justified.rationale: Proponents defend liberal-democratic order and mainstream institutions, so revolution is inferred to be disfavored.

central-planning.rationale: Sharansky, a former Soviet dissident, shapes the concept; distrust of command systems is inferred but economic views are not stated.

land-value-tax.rationale: Georgist tax policy is not discussed.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Estate taxation is not addressed; adherents split by party.

basic-income.rationale: Basic income is unrelated to the concept.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Distributist property ideas are not discussed.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: No source takes this up, but the doctrine's liberal-democratic proponents would plainly reject abolishing money.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; mainstream proponents are inferred not to favor such a radical monetary change.

experts-over-public.rationale: Technocracy is not addressed; adherents split.

one-party-rule.rationale: Proponents present the cause as defending democratic values, and a former Soviet dissident leads the framing, so one-party rule is inferred to be rejected.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between republicans and constitutional-monarchy countries.

democracy-best.rationale: Sharansky says antisemitism threatens all democratic values; a pro-democracy stance is inferred, though the sources do not discuss voters choosing badly.

direct-votes.rationale: Referendum policy is not discussed; adherents hold no shared view.

workers-councils.rationale: Not addressed; liberal-democratic proponents are inferred to prefer parliaments.

natural-rulers.rationale: The concept rests on universal equality against ethnic hierarchy, so the idea of natural rulers is inferred to be rejected.

political-violence-never.rationale: Adherents accept self-defense and counter-terror, and Sharansky stresses terrorism against Jews as the problem, so an absolute pacifist line is inferred to be rejected.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed; inferred disagreement from the liberal framing.

separate-church-state.rationale: Proponents frame the concern in secular rights language; mild agreement is inferred, though religious proponents differ.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Not addressed; secular-liberal framing suggests disagreement, with religious adherents dissenting.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from reliance on state action against antisemitism.

military-superiority.rationale: Not stated in sources; proponents are generally strong supporters of Israel's security, so mild agreement is inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Adherents back Israel as a Jewish nation-state yet frame antisemitism as bigotry against ethnic hierarchy, so they split on the general principle.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Not addressed; the concept treats antisemitism as an old hatred recurring in new forms, not class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Distributive equality is not addressed; adherents range from liberal to conservative.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Adherents claim Jews as an indigenous people of Israel, yet the general principle is not addressed.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; calling Israel a colonial project is treated as delegitimization, which suggests hostility to anti-colonial reparations framing.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed; inferred disagreement from pluralist framing.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Ethical egoism is not discussed; no position can be inferred.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The concept appeals to human rights and universal values, so duties-over-rights is inferred to be disfavored.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental ethics is unrelated to the concept.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Western-modernist framing.

human-enhancement.rationale: Transhumanist issues are unrelated to the concept.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption policy is not addressed; adherents split on security versus privacy.

restore-past-order.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from reform-oriented liberal framing.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Pragmatism versus ideology is not discussed.

direct-action.rationale: Not addressed; proponents lean toward institutional and legal remedies such as laws and state linkage.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Obviously outside the concept; modern-liberal proponents would reject it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not addressed; inferred rejection by mainstream proponents.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Communist distribution is not discussed; adherents range widely.

production-for-use.rationale: Socialist production principle is not addressed.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Not addressed; the concept treats anti-capitalist conspiracy tropes about Jews as antisemitic, so Marxist exploitation claims are inferred to be disfavored.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: A former Soviet dissident's framing and liberal proponents imply rejection.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not addressed; anti-capitalist framings of Israel are often cited as antisemitic, so disagreement is inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; liberal proponents likely accept it, though the concept limits some speech.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Adherents defend Jewish collective self-determination, so the statement splits them.

conscription.rationale: Adherents from Israel accept conscription while diaspora liberals vary, so split.

positive-liberty.rationale: Liberty theory is not discussed; adherents differ.

media-academia-power.rationale: Proponents criticize campus and media bias against Israel but not as holding more power than elected officials, so split.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The concept opposes racial antisemitism, the older wave from which it is distinguished, so racial hierarchy is inferred to be rejected.

total-state.rationale: Inferred rejection from the liberal-democratic framing and Sharansky's Soviet experience.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; mainstream proponents defend Israel's right to exist, not expansion as a principle.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Not addressed; plainly outside the liberal framing.

bound-labor.rationale: Not addressed; plainly rejected by any liberal-democratic proponent.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Proponents appeal to universal standards such as the 3D test and criticize double standards, which implies belief in neutral standards.

universal-morality.rationale: The 3D test presumes that the same moral principles should apply to Israel as to others; agreement is inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: Political philosophy of the common good is not addressed.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The 3D test treats denying Israel's right to exist, the only people denied it, as delegitimization and the IHRA definition lists denying Jews self-determination as antisemitic.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Defending Israel's Jewish character implies support for the Law of Return, though the sources do not discuss it directly.

revive-national-language.rationale: Revived Hebrew is Zionist history, but the sources never state this as a general principle, so adherents are treated as split.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Corporate governance is outside the concept.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance is not discussed; adherents split by party.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is unrelated to the concept.

economic-freedom.rationale: The link of political and economic liberty is not addressed.

national-self-determination.rationale: The IHRA definition counts denial of Jewish self-determination as antisemitic and Sharansky calls the denial of Israel's right to exist a denial no other people faces.

force-without-un.rationale: Sharansky criticizes UN double standards, so adherents are inferred to accept acting without Security Council approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Epistemology is not addressed; religious and secular adherents differ.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Workfare is not discussed; adherents split by party.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred rejection since the concept values preserving memory and heritage.

dominated-front.rationale: Sharansky says anti-Americanism and anti-Westernism have become hard to separate from antisemitism, so adherents oppose anti-Western fronts.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed; mild inferred disagreement from liberal framing.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; economic antisemitism tropes are condemned, so usury bans are inferred to be rejected.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The concept descends from opposing racial antisemitism, and its proponents argue that calling Israel apartheid is a smear, which implies hostility to real racial segregation.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is unrelated to the concept.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy myths about hidden powers are the signature of the antisemitism the concept targets, and this statement is of that form.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed by the sources.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Feminist structural analysis is not addressed; adherents split.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Populist anti-elitism is not addressed; adherents split.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is a racial-antisemitic tradition, so rejection is inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; proponents defend Israeli forces against what they call demonization but also accept accountability.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Minimal-state theory is not discussed; adherents range from libertarian to social-democratic.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Inferred rejection from opposition to racial antisemitism.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Sharansky says antisemitism threatens all democratic values, and the concept's critique of double standards rests on equal treatment.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Marxist strategy debate is outside the sources.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Describing Israel as a colonial or racist project is a standard example of delegitimization in the 3D test, and Cotler counts it among the new antisemitism's forms.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed; Israel itself has religious personal-status law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; liberal religious freedom is inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Soviet-era state theory is not addressed by the sources.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the democratic-values framing.

population-transfer.rationale: Proponents treat claims of Jews as an alien minority as antisemitic; population transfer is inferred to be rejected.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not addressed; proponents accept preemptive security measures.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Not addressed; social-Darwinist framing is part of the racial antisemitism the concept follows.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; proponents urge states to act against antisemitic movements.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican liberty theory is not addressed.

separated-powers.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic-values framing.

vanguard-party.rationale: Inferred rejection by liberal-democratic proponents and Soviet-dissident founder.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Distributive priorities are not discussed; adherents split.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: British housing policy is unrelated to the sources.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Not addressed; some Europe-focused proponents blame immigrant communities for antisemitism, but most reject this broad claim.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Not addressed; Cotler's stress on free speech and rights suggests wariness.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price-control policy is unrelated to the concept.

party-controls-media.rationale: Inferred rejection; Sharansky condemns state-controlled media that spreads antisemitic cartoons.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization rules are not discussed; adherents split.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Not addressed; Sharansky criticizes European governments' weakness but the question is broader.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Presidential versus parliamentary design is not discussed.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is unrelated to the concept.

clerical-rule.rationale: Not addressed; the concept targets Islamist antisemitism and liberal proponents would reject clerical rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not addressed; proponents strongly support national defense.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed; but proponents condemn antisemitic cartoons, so split on censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not discussed; adherents live under different systems.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Not addressed; proponents favor Western alliances and Israel's ties with the US.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not discussed; abolishing renting is a radical idea that mainstream proponents would be expected to reject.

people-in-arms.rationale: Militia theory is not addressed; adherents hold no common view.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is not addressed by the sources.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Anti-intellectual populism is not discussed; adherents split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not addressed; adherents criticize Arab-media antisemitism as bad yet value pluralism.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Sex education is unrelated; religious and secular adherents split.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not discussed; mainstream liberal and Jewish-communal proponents are inferred to oppose teaching creationism.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Israel's Law of Return gives descent-based entry, but sources do not address citizenship rules.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religious-liberty exemptions are not addressed; Jewish groups differ on them.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Debt relief is outside the concept.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Neocolonial economics is not addressed; adherents hold no shared view.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Foreign aid duties are not addressed; adherents split.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Constitutional design is never discussed by the sources, and adherents live under many different systems.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are outside the concept and adherents hold no shared view.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Proponents are divided between those who accept territorial compromise and those like Sharansky who condition concessions on democracy; sources do not settle it.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property theory is never discussed; adherents range from libertarian to social-democratic.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Sharansky, a Soviet dissident, saw the USSR as a totalitarian tyranny, but the state-capitalist label is a Marxist-theory question the sources never raise.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is outside the concept.

collective-defense.rationale: Proponents are pro-Western and favor alliances, though the sources do not discuss NATO-style pacts.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The concept is about antisemitism, and adherents differ on whether Israel's control of territory is occupation.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church-state relations are not discussed beyond antisemitism, and adherents split.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not discussed; no shared position on ceremonial heads of state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The sources never discuss secession, and adherents have no common view.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A sacred divine ruler is incompatible with the democratic framing the sources use; inferred rather than stated.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax design is outside the concept.

character-from-environment.rationale: Not addressed, though the concept rejects racial determinism, adherents need not take a stance on nature versus nurture.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred rejection from the rule-of-law and democratic-values framing in Sharansky's essay.

space-expansion.rationale: Not discussed and unrelated to the concept.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is not addressed by the sources.

leader-cult.rationale: Sharansky is a former Soviet dissident and his essay opposes totalitarian propaganda cults, so rejection is inferred.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family law is outside the concept.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The statement is internal Marxist theory that the sources never address, so mild disagreement is only inferred.

land-redistribution.rationale: Agrarian policy is unrelated to the concept.

refugee-return.rationale: The sources do not discuss this, but a Palestinian right of return is widely seen by adherents as threatening Israel's Jewish character, which fits their delegitimization concern.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Not discussed, but proponents defend existing state boundaries and Israel's legitimacy rather than irredentism.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred from the liberal rights framing and from opposition to Islamist rule that the sources document.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from the liberal rights framing, with no source on the topic.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Not discussed, but pan-ethnic unions such as pan-Arabism are not part of the concept's liberal outlook.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Proponents back a Jewish state rather than diaspora autonomy, though the sources never discuss it, so disagreement is inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Adherents back Israel as a refuge, yet the concept defends Jewish communities abroad too, so a mild disagree is inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The concept treats antisemitism as a persistent hatred changing forms, not an epiphenomenon of the economy, so mild disagreement is inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank-rescue policy is never discussed by the sources and adherents differ by party.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred from democratic-values framing that includes rights protections.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas are not discussed and adherents split.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Cotler treats economic boycotts as antisemitic, so closed economic blocs are inferred to be disfavored.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred rejection of insurgent theory by liberal-democratic proponents who see terrorism as the problem.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Not discussed, but the concept rests on equal standards and treating no group as lesser.

patriotic-education.rationale: Adherents split between diaspora liberals and Israeli patriots; no source speaks to it.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: American proponents such as the ADL have taken varied positions, and the sources do not discuss it.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary-system reform is never discussed by the sources; adherents hold no shared view.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Economic theory is outside the concept.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Post-imperial influence policy is outside the sources; no shared view.

delink-world-market.rationale: Cotler treats economic boycott as antisemitic, so economic delinking is inferred to be disfavored.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Not discussed, but proponents oppose discrimination against Jews, so mild disagreement is inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not discussed; the concept rejects colonial framings of Israel.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred from the democratic framing, though the sources do not discuss hereditary rule.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Elite duty is not discussed; no position can be inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The concept urges active political engagement against antisemitism, so withdrawal is inferred to be disfavored.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Frankfurt-style media critique is not part of the concept; adherents split.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony is never addressed by the sources.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The concept associates anti-capitalist and Third-Worldist narratives with the new antisemitism, so disagreement is inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices for native-born citizens echoes the dual-loyalty libel the IHRA definition lists as antisemitic, so rejection is inferred.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development policy is outside the concept; no shared view.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Revanchism is not discussed; adherents hold no common position.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaty rights of internal nations are not addressed.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Communitarian utopias are not addressed; no inference possible.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Third-way economics is not addressed; adherents split.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Adherents rest the Jewish claim to Israel partly on historical ties, but the sources do not state the general principle, so the agreement is mild.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Cotler's list of the new antisemitism's forms includes Holocaust denial, and the IHRA definition lists claims that Jews or Israel invented or exaggerated the Holocaust.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not discussed; Western liberal proponents would reject it.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred from the liberal framing and from the focus on Islamist antisemitism, with no direct source.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Sharansky documents calls to terrorism in Arab state media, but the sources do not address this doctrine itself.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred rejection, since the concept targets Islamist movements.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Participatory theory is not discussed; adherents differ.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Proponents dispute that intersectional movements treat Jews fairly, so mild disagreement is inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Gender-identity law is unrelated; adherents split.

assisted-dying.rationale: Medical ethics is unrelated to the concept; adherents split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The concept locates antisemitism on the far left, far right and Islamism alike, but not a claim that the axis is obsolete.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxian alienation theory is not discussed.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Some proponents fault Muslim immigrant communities (Fischel), but most reject calling Islam as such incompatible, so mild disagreement.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Dress rules are not addressed; French and American proponents differ.

social-market-economy.rationale: Economic-model choice is not addressed; adherents split.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Adherents defend Israel's right to self-defense, so abolishing armies is inferred to be rejected.

rich-first.rationale: Development sequencing is outside the sources.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Proponents lean toward Western alignment, so neutrality is inferred to be disfavored.

worker-ownership.rationale: Worker ownership is unrelated to the concept, and adherents run from social democrats to market conservatives.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Not discussed; proponents hold liberal equal-standards views and reject colonial exploitation, though the sources never address it.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The thesis does not address succession; inferred from its adherents' loyalty to democratic states.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The thesis concerns antisemitism, not banking; its adherents span left to right.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range across the political spectrum on international lenders.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred from proponents' commitment to democratic equality; the sources do not discuss franchise.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not addressed by the thesis, and adherents are split.

reification.rationale: Not addressed by the thesis; adherents include both Marxist and anti-Marxist thinkers.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Not addressed by the thesis; adherents range from left to right on media ownership.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred from proponents' commitment to liberal democratic norms; the sources do not state it.

racial-franchise.rationale: Proponents define antisemitism as discrimination and see exclusion by descent as its core form, and the IHRA definition opposes racism; they would reject a racial franchise.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic to the thesis; adherents are split.

open-government-data.rationale: Not addressed by the thesis; adherents are split.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Adherents are divided, as Israeli marriage law is itself contested; the thesis does not address it.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Boycotts targeting Jews or Jewish businesses are a classic antisemitic act, and the IHRA examples and 3D test count discriminatory targeting of Jews as antisemitism.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not addressed by the thesis; adherents are split.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Not addressed by the thesis; adherents include religious and secular people.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Wealth inequality is outside the thesis; proponents span left-liberal to conservative and have no common line.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The concept concerns antisemitism, not military policy; proponents divide along ordinary party lines.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred: proponents list Soviet-style and Islamist state hostility to Jews and religion among sources of the problem and defend Jewish communal life, so state-promoted unbelief is unlikely to be backed.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred: proponents press states to police antisemitic incidents and crime and seek protection for Jewish institutions, so abolishing police is unlikely; the sources do not address it directly.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed; proponents divide on this and the thesis says nothing on government structure.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Unrelated to the thesis; proponents divide along ordinary party lines.

term-limits.rationale: Unrelated to the thesis; proponents divide along ordinary party lines.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: proponents work within representative democracies and call for state action, and nothing in the sources suggests support for delegable voting.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed; proponents have no common view.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Unrelated to the thesis; proponents include members of both egalitarian and traditional faiths.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred: mainstream proponents are in modern liberal democracies, where shared authority is the norm, but the thesis does not address it and traditional adherents differ.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The thesis concerns hostility to Israel and Jews; residents' voting rights are outside it and proponents are split.

rent-control.rationale: Not related to the thesis; proponents are drawn from across the spectrum.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: mainstream proponents are mostly conventional liberal and conservative; not discussed in the sources.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: the proponents' liberal-democratic framing of civil society makes state-run uniformed youth unlikely.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; proponents hold differing views on nuclear policy.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; proponents are split on foreign bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: proponents center the Holocaust and condemn denial of historical atrocities, but state recognition of genocide generally is not discussed.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Unrelated to the thesis; proponents span left and right.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: proponents defend Israel's right to defend itself, implying lethal self-defence is legitimate.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between historical-continuity and constructed views of nations.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred: mainstream proponents are mostly conventional liberals or conservatives; the question was not addressed.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Unrelated to the thesis; proponents are split.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: proponents condemn glorification of those who die in attacks on civilians, so sacralising national martyrs is not their line.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred: the 3D test frames antisemitism as a civic-political wrong judged by standards, not as cosmic struggle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred: proponents hold that Israel is the Jewish people's national home, not only a cultural centre; they differ on diaspora roles.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred: they defend Israel's statehood and judge denial of a state to one people as delegitimization, i.e. state before cultural renewal.

god-not-male.rationale: Unrelated to the thesis; proponents include different religious and secular views.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Unrelated to the thesis; proponents include religious and secular views.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Economic-control tropes about Jews are classic antisemitism in the IHRA examples and proponents' own warnings.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not related to the thesis; not addressed by the sources.

independent-unions.rationale: Proponents are mostly liberal democrats who value independent civil society; not discussed directly, so inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The thesis concerns antisemitism, not the meaning of socialism; adherents span the political spectrum.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not an issue for the thesis; adherents span left and right so no common line.

second-chamber.rationale: Not an issue for the thesis; adherents split by national tradition.

municipal-property.rationale: Proponents mostly belong to liberal and conservative camps that favour private or national ownership; inferred, not stated.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Not an issue for the thesis; adherents span left and right.

family-wage.rationale: Not an issue for the thesis; adherents span left and right.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not an issue for the thesis; no common line.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not an issue for the thesis; no common line.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not an issue for the thesis; adherents are split on privacy and state oversight, though some favour tracing extremist funding.

online-anonymity.rationale: Proponents split: some call for identifying online abusers while others defend anonymity; the thesis does not address it.

person-over-state.rationale: Sharansky's liberal test of a free society values individual dignity against state power, but the sources do not state this directly.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Not an issue for the thesis; adherents span secular and religious.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not an issue for the thesis; no common line.

gm-crops.rationale: Not an issue for the thesis; no common line.

dense-cities.rationale: Not an issue for the thesis; no common line.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Proponents oppose racial hatred but defend Jewish collective self-determination as a national right; adherents split on group organising, so unstated.

racial-pride.rationale: Proponents defend pride in Jewish identity and peoplehood as legitimate and oppose stigmatising it, as the Israel-related examples of the IHRA definition imply.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Proponents defend Israel's right to defend itself but split on wider uses of force; the thesis does not address it.

missingStatements.text: Denying one nation's right to a state of its own, while accepting that right for other nations, is a form of prejudice.
missingStatements.rationale: Delegitimization, the denial to Israel of a right granted to every other people, is one of Sharansky's three markers and an IHRA example.

missingStatements.text: A government's conduct should be judged by the same standards as every other government's, and singling out one state for condemnation shows bias.
missingStatements.rationale: The double-standards limb of the 3D test turns on singling Israel out at the UN while ignoring states such as China, Iran, Cuba and Syria.
missingStatements.declined: Near-universal principle of equal standards; would not discriminate between ideologies.

missingStatements.text: Comparing a contemporary democratic government's policies to those of Nazi Germany is illegitimate.
missingStatements.rationale: Sharansky counts comparing Israelis to Nazis as demonization, and the IHRA definition lists it as an example of antisemitism.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow to the Israel debate and already partly covered by Zionism-related statements; too niche.

notes: Proponents divide on how far criticism of Israeli policy is safe: Cotler calls equating anti-Zionism per se with antisemitism too simplistic, whereas Sharansky's test treats the three Ds as sufficient. Critics (Klug, Finkelstein, Lerman, Bauer) deny that the phenomenon is new or that it is antisemitism rather than political dispute. A very large share of the answers are low-confidence inferences.
